plain.li: [winter] Hot porridge with honey this morning, while the frost was still on the window.
[summer] Cold meat and fresh greens for supper, too hot for anything else. It was just right.
[spring] The first fresh greens of the year in the stew tonight. They tasted of the field.
[spring] Eggs for breakfast, and enough to go round for once.
[fall] Supper from the new harvest tonight, with more on the table than we could finish.
[fall] Baked roots and smoked meat after a day in the fields. I slept the moment I lay down.
[hurt] Someone cut my meat for me without being asked. It was a good supper, and I ate all of it.
[skill:Cooking] Ate a dish I'd never thought to make. I'm going to try it myself, with a few changes.
Ate with my back to the wall and my feet up, and not one person needed me for the whole meal.

warm.li: The cook remembered I don't like onions and left them out of my bowl. Small thing. I noticed.
Good supper, and good company at the table. I stayed long after my bowl was empty.

blunt.li: Meat, bread, gravy. That's a meal.
Ate well. Slept well after. Good day.

cheerful.li: Supper was so good I licked the spoon, and then the bowl, when nobody was looking!
Fresh bread tonight, still warm. I had three slices and I'd do it again.

gloomy.li: A fine supper. I ate it as if it might be the last good one for a while.
Good food tonight. I'd almost forgotten what that was like.

cold.li: The meal was well made. I'll eat whatever that cook makes from now on.
Good food, served hot and on time. That's rarer here than it should be.

plain.li: [winter] Long dark evening, so {OTHER_nameDef} and I talked until the candle guttered. I learned where {OTHER_pronoun} grew up.
[spring] Planting all day beside {OTHER_nameDef}, talking the whole time. The rows came out crooked.
[summer] Too hot to sleep, so {OTHER_nameDef} and I sat outside and talked until the air cooled.
[summer] Lay on the roof with {OTHER_nameDef} after dark and talked about the stars and the people under them.
[fall] Brought in the harvest beside {OTHER_nameDef}, and we talked about the years we'd want to forget.
[fall] Leaves coming down, and {OTHER_nameDef} and I walked the long way back so we could keep talking.
[rain] Rain on the roof, and {OTHER_nameDef} told me about the worst storm {OTHER_pronoun} ever lived through.
[skill:Social] {OTHER_nameDef} usually keeps to {OTHER_objective}self, but tonight {OTHER_nameDef} talked and I mostly listened.
[newcomer] {OTHER_nameDef} asked where I came from and actually wanted to know. I talked more than I have since I got here.

warm.li: Sat up late with {OTHER_nameDef}, talking about the people we love. Some of them are here and some aren't.
I told {OTHER_nameDef} something I was ashamed of, and {OTHER_pronoun} didn't flinch.

blunt.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} half the night. Tired today. Worth it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I traded stories about our worst haircuts and laughed until we couldn't breathe.
I found out {OTHER_nameDef} used to want to be a singer! I've asked for a song tomorrow.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I talked about the friends we've buried, one at a time, by name.
Talked late with {OTHER_nameDef}, with the lamp out. I said things I wouldn't have said with it lit.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} told me about {OTHER_possessive} family tonight. I'll be careful with what I know now.
A long talk with {OTHER_nameDef}. I said less than {OTHER_pronoun} did, which is how I prefer it.

plain.li: [good] The path to the fields has been swept and lined with stones. It's a nicer walk than it was.
[bad] Somebody left a heap of dirty rags by the kitchen door, and it's been there since yesterday.

warm.li: [good] Someone put a sprig of flowers on the supper table. I moved it so I could see it from my seat.
[good] The hall looks lovely since the new rug went down. I sat on it with my back to the wall for a while.
[bad] Picked up the scraps by the door on my way past. Somebody has to start.
[bad] The place has gotten shabby, but I don't blame anyone. We've all been so busy.

blunt.li: [good] Nice walls. Nice floor. Don't wreck it.
[good] Someone made the hall look decent. Good.
[bad] Bones in the yard. Who leaves bones in the yard?

cheerful.li: [good] There's a new carving by the door, and I patted it on the head on my way past!
[good] The garden's blooming, and the hall smells of flowers. I could live in this hall.
[bad] Mud everywhere, so I've started calling the hall the swamp. Somebody laughed!
[bad] The place is a mess, but I scrubbed one window, and it sparkles.

gloomy.li: [good] It's pretty here now. That only makes it worse to think about losing it.
[good] The painting in the hall is good. I stood in front of it longer than I meant to.
[bad] Stains on the floor and a wall half built. About how I feel.
[bad] The hall hasn't been cleaned in days. Maybe none of us has the heart.

cold.li: [good] The colony looks cared for. Cared-for places are better defended.
[good] The new art is well placed. I'll grant the sculptor that.
[bad] The yard is a mess. I've started noting who walks past it without picking anything up.
[bad] Dirt spreads if it's left. I've written down where it started.

plain.li: [good] Changed the straw in my mattress today. Slept like a stone.
[bad] The shutter in my room creaks every time the wind picks up. I lay awake waiting for it.

warm.li: [good] My room's small, but it's mine, and I've put the things people gave me where I can see them.
[good] Fell asleep tonight feeling safe, in a room I'm starting to love.
[bad] My room needs work, but I've got time, and people have offered to help.
[bad] Slept badly again in that poky room. I'll mention it tomorrow, nicely.

blunt.li: [bad] Cold, damp and small. Not a room. A cupboard.
[bad] Slept badly again. It's the room.

cheerful.li: [good] My bed is the best place in the world, and I'm not getting out of it until breakfast smells ready.
[good] Woke to sunlight on my wall and a bird outside the window. Perfect morning!
[bad] My room's cold, so I've built a nest of every blanket I own. It's actually lovely.
[bad] Small room, but I've decided it's snug!

gloomy.li: [good] Slept well for once. I don't trust it.
[good] The room is nice. I lay in it and didn't think about anything, which hasn't happened in a while.
[bad] Woke in the dark and couldn't remember where I was, and then I did, and that was worse.
[bad] Four walls, a damp bed and the sound of someone snoring through the wall.

cold.li: [good] Good room, good rest. I'll be sharper tomorrow for it.
[good] I've arranged the room so I can see the door from the bed. I slept well.
[bad] The room is badly built. I could do better in an afternoon, and I may have to.
[bad] A poor room means poor sleep, and poor sleep means mistakes. I've raised it.
